area: The first eight seconds — hero, headline, and what a stranger can actually see above the fold
diagnosis:
READ AS A STRANGER, TOP TO BOTTOM. What is literally on screen before I scroll: a nav bar, an eyebrow reading "Free · Open source · MIT · Windows", the headline "Everything you need mid-game, and nothing you have to take on faith.", a four-line paragraph, two buttons, the line "Windows 10 & 11 · no account · no telemetry", and one screenshot. That is the entire first impression. Here is what is wrong with each piece. 1. THE HEADLINE ARGUES BEFORE IT INTRODUCES. "Everything you need mid-game, and nothing you have to take on faith." — Half of this sentence is a rebuttal to an accusation I have not made. "nothing you have to take on faith" only lands on someone who already distrusts op.gg and u.gg. I have never heard of you; I have no grievance for you to answer. You are winning an argument I am not having. Meanwhile "mid-game" is ambiguous in exactly the worst way — next to a brand called AllMid it reads as *mid lane*, so my first inference is "a tool for mid-laners." And count the category nouns in that headline: zero. No "League of Legends", no "tier list", no "builds", no "counters", no "overlay", no number. Fourteen words that could sit on top of a productivity SaaS. 2. THE LEDE BURIES ITS BEST SENTENCE IN POSITION FOUR. "A League of Legends companion that reads your own client, sets your masteries before the timer runs out, and puts objective timers on top of the game." — "companion" is a category word with no payload. "reads your own client" is meant as a trust feature and reads, cold, as *this thing reads my client* — that is the sentence structure of a keylogger disclosure, not a benefit. Then comes "because a win rate without a sample size is just a number that looks like an answer," which is the single best line on this page, and it is spent on a reader who has already decided. Thirty-eight words in, still no number, still nothing I can check. 3. THE ONE IMAGE IN THE HERO CONTRADICTS THE PAGE. This is the most damaging thing on the site and it is not a copy problem. `img/app/allmid-main.png` shows the app's own title bar reading **"111,728 games"**. Everywhere else the page says **125,096 games**. The entire pitch is "our numbers are honest and carry their sample size" and the hero image disagrees with the hero copy by 13,368 games. Any visitor who notices has been handed a reason to distrust you by the one asset meant to build trust. And that is before what the screenshot actually shows. The status card says **"In the lobby."** The rank badge says **"Wood IV 90 LP."** Below it is a match history of one player's Ashe games, some of them 1-minute and 9-minute remakes with 0/0/0 and 0.5k gold. The only stat visible is "60% (20)" — a twenty-game sample, which is precisely the thing your own copy calls "noise wearing a percentage." So the hero image sells: a match-history list every League player already gets free inside their client, belonging to a Wood IV account, currently doing nothing. There is no tier list in it, no build, no counter, no overlay. The product's actual differentiator appears nowhere in the only picture of the product. 4. THERE IS NO DATA ABOVE THE FOLD. AT ALL. The only digit in the first screen is "173", and it is inside a button label — "Browse 173 champions" — and 173 is Riot's champion count, not your achievement. 125,096 does not appear until I scroll. You own 125,096 recorded Classic games, 362,263 players, 1,250,960 counted player slots, 2,028 matchups over 100 games, and a 15.6-point spread between the best and worst champion in the mode. A stranger sees none of it. Meanwhile every competitor I would compare you against puts a ranked tier list with win rates directly on the front page. You put an aphorism there. This matters more here than for a normal stats site, because your data is *strange*. Blitzcrank is the #2 mid-laner at 59.2% over 3,209 games. Wukong mid is 60.8%. Janna is the best support at 55.8% over 8,190. Any League player who sees a mid-lane list headed by Blitzcrank stops scrolling and asks what this data set is. That reaction is the desire the owner says the site fails to create, and it is sitting unused in meta.json. 5. THE SECOND SCROLL-STOP IS A LIST OF THINGS YOU DON'T HAVE. Immediately below the hero: "Queues — Classic 125,096 games · Ranked Solo/Duo **no data yet** · Flex **no data yet** · Normal Draft **no data yet** · ARAM **no data yet**." Four-fifths of that bar is absence, and it is placed at the exact moment I am deciding whether this is a real product. Honesty is the brand and I would not remove it, but it belongs after I have been shown what you *do* have, not before. 6. THEN SIX EMPTY BOXES. The "Six things it does" grid renders `Champion select` six times — a styled placeholder with a word in it. Six consecutive empty frames read as one sentence: *unfinished*. Combined with four "no data yet" chips, the first two screens after the hero communicate "not ready" more clearly than anything else on the page. 7. SMALL, REAL DEFECTS THAT COMPOUND. `id="overlay"` appears twice (on the feature `
` and on the overlay `
`), so `#overlay` is ambiguous. Two separate IntersectionObserver blocks run at the bottom, one adding `.in` and one adding `.op` — the second is dead leftover, with its own 3-second `setTimeout` fallback duplicating the first's 2.5-second one. WHY I WOULD CLOSE THE TAB: in eight seconds I learned that something is free, open-source and Windows-only, that it doesn't want me to take things on faith, and that a Wood IV player has been losing on Ashe. I did not learn what it computes, what it knows that nobody else knows, or a single number I could check. The site spends its opening on epistemology while sitting on the only Classic data set in existence. THE SMALLEST SET OF CHANGES WITH THE LARGEST EFFECT, in order: (a) Put the real tier list in the hero, in place of the screenshot. Fixes the missing data, the missing product, the missing proof, and deletes the 111,728-vs-125,096 contradiction in one move. **Built below.** (b) Rewrite the headline and lede so the first line names the gap and carries the number. **Built below.** (c) Add a three-figure proof strip under the CTAs, and demote the "win rate without a sample size" line to its caption — where it sits beside real sample sizes and is *demonstrated* instead of asserted. **Built below.** (d) Move `${modusBalk()}` (the four "no data yet" chips) to below the `#classic-spot` section so absence follows evidence. One-line move, included below. (e) Retake the screenshots. Not code — see imageRequests. I built (a)–(d) as one replacement hero, driven entirely by champions.json and meta.json. Nothing in it is typed by hand.

area: The homepage hero (.lol-held in site/build.mjs, leaguePagina())
diagnosis: The hero currently sells a mood, not a product. Concretely: (1) The only proof of the software existing is one 1296x828 screenshot parked in the right column with no caption, no framing claim, and no indication it is a real capture rather than a placeholder — and the six feature blocks below it are empty, so this single image is carrying the entire "does this software exist" burden and is not asked to. (2) The first screen contains exactly zero rows of data. The project owns 125,096 recorded games, 63 champions with qualified per-lane win rates, and a lane-by-lane tier list already computed by tierFor() — and none of it is above the fold. A visitor comparing us to op.gg or u.gg sees their tier list immediately and sees ours only after two scrolls, on a different page (classic.html#tiers). (3) The headline "Everything you need mid-game, and nothing you have to take on faith" is a posture, not a claim — it names no capability and carries no number. The 125,096 figure does not appear until the third section down. (4) The lede is 48 words of argument about sample sizes before the reader has been told what the program does. (5) The battlefield image is the loudest element on the screen: hero-bg.png renders at full opacity behind a scrim tuned only to protect the left column, so the brightest region of the composition is the burning base on the right, competing directly with the app screenshot. (6) mosaicTiles() emits 54 splash-art tags into a container that CSS unconditionally sets to display:none — dead weight on the most performance-critical screen of the site. The fix is not more atmosphere: it is to put the software and its numbers on the first screen, and demote the battlefield to ground.

area: Competitive teardown → proposed homepage section order for site/index.html, plus the highest-impact section built: a live, lane-tabbed League Classic tier list with the real most-built core per row.
diagnosis:
WHY THE PAGE DOES NOT CREATE DESIRE

The homepage renders 27 KB. Of that, the total quantity of dataset on it is four numbers in one grey tile row (`spotcijfers`) and the string "125,096 games" repeated three times in prose. There is not one champion name, win rate, item, or table. Meanwhile the repo is sitting on 125,096 games, 1,250,960 parsed player slots, 296 lane build entries, and 63 champion pages that already exist and already render well — all of it on classic.html and champions.html, i.e. behind a click that a first-time visitor has no reason to make.

Three specific failures:

1. THE ASSET IS BURIED. `tierFor()`, `tierLists()`, `findings()`, `rosterStrip()`, `explorerGrid()` and `detailPanel()` are all written, tested and shipping — on classic.html only. leaguePagina() calls exactly two of the data functions (`mosaicTiles`, and a 14-icon `voorbeeld` slice). Every competitor in this category leads with the table: op.gg and u.gg put the search field and a champion tier list above the fold; blitz.gg puts the product screenshot above the fold and the meta tables one screen down. We put a headline and a paragraph. A visitor who arrives from a Discord link and leaves in eight seconds has seen zero evidence.

2. THE PRODUCT IS INVISIBLE, AND THE PLACEHOLDERS ARE WORSE THAN NOTHING. `KENMERKEN` has six entries pointing at img/app/champion-select.png, overlay.png, builds.png, matchups.png, sample.png, privacy.png. Only `allmid-main.png` exists. So `kenmerkBlok()` renders six `<span class="kenmerk-wacht">` grey rectangles in a row, in the section headed "Six things it does". The page's largest block is six empty boxes labelled with the features they are failing to show. Six empty frames do not read as "screenshots pending", they read as "vapourware". One empty frame would cost a sixth as much.
   Worth flagging: real screenshots DO exist on disk and nothing renders them — site/img/app/_masteries.png, _meta.png, _probe.png, _runes.png, site/img/champion-select.png, docs/screenshots/champion-select.png, docs/screenshots/meta.png, and site/img/app/builds.png (appeared during this session). At least three of the six blocks can be filled by renaming files, today, with no new capture work.

3. THERE IS NO PROOF LAYER, ONLY ASSERTION. "125,096 games" is a claim of exactly the same evidential weight as "trusted by millions". What converts is not the size of the number, it is the visible machinery behind it: a raw column next to a smoothed column, a qualifier count per lane, a collection window with dates, the smoothing formula printed in the open. All of that exists in `tierLists()`'s footnote — on the other page. The homepage's honesty pitch ("nothing you have to take on faith") is currently asserted in prose and demonstrated nowhere, which is the exact inversion of the brand.

---

WHAT A CONVERTING GAMING-ANALYTICS HOMEPAGE DOES

The sequence the four competitors converge on, and the reason for each beat:

- op.gg / u.gg (data-first): search field → champion tier list / meta tables → deeper stats → desktop-app banner near the bottom. They give value before they ask for anything. The download is a consequence of the data being good, not a precondition for seeing it.
- blitz.gg / mobalytics (product-first): hero with a real product screenshot + download → scale claim → feature blocks, each one a real screenshot of the running app → safety/legitimacy → download again.

Both shapes obey the same rule: DEMONSTRATE, THEN ASK. Neither ever shows a frame with nothing in it. AllMid's position is unusual and better than either: we are product-first (there is an installer) but our data is genuinely unobtainable elsewhere, because Riot's public API does not carry Classic. That makes the table our strongest single asset, not a supporting one — it is the only thing on the site that literally cannot be found anywhere else. It therefore goes directly under the hero, ahead of the product tour.

---

PROPOSED SECTION ORDER FOR index.html

1. TOOLBAR + SEARCH — `toolbalk("home")`, unchanged. The champion search field (`zoekIndex()` + `ZOEK_SCRIPT`, 173 names) already exists and is our answer to op.gg's summoner search. Keep it visible, do not collapse it behind an icon.

2. HERO — keep, but cut the lede's second half. Keep `heldBeeld` (img/app/allmid-main.png exists, so it is a real screenshot). Earns position: one claim, one product image, one download button.

3. **LIVE TIER LIST — NEW. THIS IS THE SECTION I BUILT BELOW.** Lane tabs, top 10 per lane, win rate + raw + games + pick rate + the boots-and-three-item core those players actually bought, plus a six-tile proof strip (games, player slots, players, champions, patches, newest game). Fills from `tierFor()` + `builds.json` + `T`. Earns first position after the hero because it is the only content on the site a competitor cannot replicate, and because it converts the way op.gg's front page converts: the visitor gets something useful before being asked for anything.

4. FINDINGS — call the EXISTING `findings()` verbatim. Three computed statements over splash art (strongest champion + spread, champions qualifying in all five lanes, most lopsided matchup ≥100 meetings). Zero new code. Earns its position because after a table the reader wants a conclusion, and these are conclusions no other site can draw.

5. THE ROSTER — replace the 14-icon `voorbeeld` with the EXISTING `rosterStrip()` (all 63 portraits, two edge-to-edge rows) + the link to champions.html. Zero new code. Fourteen arbitrary icons is a fragment; sixty-three is a claim. Earns its position as the visual bridge from "here is a table" to "here is coverage".

6. PRODUCT TOUR — `KENMERKEN`, CUT FROM SIX TO THREE, and gate the section on having images. Champion select, overlay, builds — the three with screenshots available now. Demoted below the data because our data is stronger than our screenshots today; promote it above the tier list the day all six screenshots exist.

7. SAFETY / "WILL I GET BANNED" — the existing `tweeluik` (on the panel / never on it). Move it HERE, after desire has been created. It answers the category's number-one objection, and an objection-handler placed before desire reads as a disclaimer.

8. WHERE THE DATA COMES FROM — the `classic-spot` prose. Keep the copy, DELETE its `spotcijfers` tile block (those four numbers now live in section 3's proof strip, where they have context). Demoted to methodology footnote position.

9. DOWNLOAD CLOSE — `band#get`, unchanged.

10. FOOTER — unchanged.

CUTS, EXPLICITLY:
- **`modusBalk()` — CUT from the homepage.** It is a row advertising three queues we do not have, forty pixels below the headline. It reads as "mostly empty product" to someone who has not yet been given a reason to care. Keep the function; it stays valid on classic.html where it is context rather than a promise. The section I wrote takes its exact slot.
- **The `voorbeeld` 14-icon strip — CUT.** Superseded by `rosterStrip()`.
- **`spotcijfers` (4 tiles in classic-spot) — CUT.** Superseded by the proof strip in section 3.
- **`KENMERKEN` entries 4–6 (matchups, sample, lokaal) — DEMOTE** out of image-framed blocks into a plain three-column text row until their screenshots exist. Never render `kenmerk-wacht` more than once on a page.
- **`kenmerk-wacht` as a pattern — RECONSIDER.** `kenmerkBlok()` should filter on `existsSync` and drop the block entirely rather than draw an empty frame. An absent section is invisible; an empty frame is a broadcast of what is missing.

---

NOTE ON THE BUILT SECTION

I patched build.mjs, ran `node site/build.mjs`, and inspected the output before reverting the tree to clean. Results: index.html 27 KB → 101 KB, build exits 0, all 242 image references inside the new section resolve to files that exist, all hrefs resolve, 5 panes, 50 data rows. Every top-10 champion in all five lanes has a `core` entry in builds.json and every core item icon exists in site/img/items — verified across all 50 rows, zero misses, so there is no fallback path in production. The 74 KB is template indentation and gzips away.

Sample of the real output (Top, rank 1): Katarina, 58.8% smoothed / 58.9% raw over 2,528 games, 1.1% pick, most built Sorcerer's Shoes → Abyssal Scepter → Rabadon's Deathcap → Hextech Gunblade over 320 games at 68.5%. That last figure is the one that sells the software, and it is real.

JS-off behaviour: all five lanes render stacked with `<h3>` headings. The tab bar is `display:none` until the inline script adds `.meta-js` to the section, at which point the tabs appear and the panes collapse to one. Progressive enhancement in the correct direction — a tab that cannot open is content that has vanished. Arrow-key navigation and roving tabindex are wired. All transitions are disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

diagnosis: index.html tells you it has 125,096 games and then shows you none of them. The whole page is claims about data: a hero paragraph, a queue bar that says "125,096 games", a stat block with four round numbers, and a link to classic.html where the actual tier list lives. A visitor who lands on allmid.gg gets zero champions, zero win rates, zero sample sizes — nothing they could not have read on a poster. Competitors put a ranked list of champions with win rates on the front page, so the first ten seconds answer "who is strong right now"; ours answers "we exist and we have a philosophy". area: The proof layer — making "125,096 games" feel real, large and hard-won (new `#proof` section on the homepage)
diagnosis: Today the dataset only ever appears as a rounded noun: "125,096 games" in a lede, four flat tiles in `.spotcijfers`, "125,096 games / 362,263 players / 63 champions / 5 lanes". Every one of those is a round assertion of the kind every competitor also prints, so the visitor's only options are to believe it or not — nothing on the page lets them check, and nothing conveys the shape or the cost of the collection. Worse, the numbers that would actually convince are already sitting unused in the data: 1,250,960 player slots that come to exactly ten per game, 164,160 slots the client could not assign a position and which are therefore excluded from every lane figure, 9 duplicate game ids dropped, 0 unparseable lines, a 24.2-day window across two named patches, a measured 1,799.6-second mean game length. Those counters are the tell that a real crawler ran over a real file — a fabricated dataset does not have a nine in it, and it certainly does not advertise the 13% of its sample it threw away. The fix is to stop asserting and open the books: one figure that shows the sample's mass and its lane distribution as 1,250 marks drawn from the true numbers, and one ledger that lists every counter, the thresholds, and the derivations, so a reader can verify the arithmetic in their head (125,096 × 10 = 1,250,960; the five lane counts plus the unpositioned ones sum exactly to that total; the six shares sum to exactly 100.00%). Note for the orchestrator: while I worked, commit 87f640a (made by another session) swept three of my scratch files into the repo — `site/.proof-test.mjs`, `.proof-test.html`, `.proof-test.css`. I have deleted them from the working tree, so they now show as unstaged deletions in `git status`; they need to be staged/committed away, and nothing else of mine touches the repo.

area: The download and conversion moment (index.html #get), app.html and overlay.html
diagnosis:
The download moment currently asks for an install without answering the only question a first-time visitor actually has. `.downloadblok` is a centred h2, one line of reassurance ("No account, no telemetry, no installer surprises"), a button and a link — four elements, all of them assertions. Nobody has ever run this .exe. The question in their head is not "do I want this" but "what happens when I click", and the page answers it with adjectives. Worse, every claim that could create desire is stated as a slogan rather than a checkable fact: "no telemetry" is exactly what spyware says. Meanwhile app.html renders six KENMERKEN blocks of which four are grey `.kenmerk-wacht` placeholders, so the page meant to sell the software is literally a page with no software in it — while two real, high-quality screenshots (`site/img/champion-select.png`, `site/img/meta.png`) and a third (`site/img/app/allmid-main.png`) sit unused in the repo because KENMERKEN points at `img/app/*.png` paths that were never created. overlay.html is a single yes/no panel with no mention of the constraint that will actually decide whether the overlay works on someone's machine (exclusive fullscreen), which means the first person who installs it, sees nothing, and concludes the app is broken was lost by an omission on this page.

The strongest asset in this repo is being thrown away: the privacy/no-injection story is not a promise here, it is a finite, enumerable list. `src/core/lcu/` is the app's entire network surface toward League, and it is nine GET endpoints plus one PATCH. Printing that table is a thing no competitor can do — Blitz, OP.GG and Overwolf cannot, because in Overwolf's case it does inject. A visitor who reads a complete endpoint list stops wondering what the app does behind their back, because the answer is on the page and they can diff it against the source. That is the proof layer this area was missing, and it converts far harder than another line of reassurance.

Second gap: the release ships with the whole community dataset compiled in, and the download moment never says so. "Download this app and start collecting" is a chore; "125,096 games, 62,534 hours of Classic, 6,808 build rows and 2,561 lane matchups are already inside it" is an arrival. Those figures are all counted from the real data files at build time, so they age with the snapshot instead of rotting into a lie.

area: Interactive moments — one genuinely useful interactive element for the homepage: "Champion select, in the page", a live replica of the app's champion-select panel driven by inline real data (63 champions x 296 ranked lanes).
diagnosis:
The homepage asks a visitor to take the product on faith. It states "125,096 games", it lists six things the app does, and it links to a champion list — but at no point does the visitor get to *use* anything. The only interactive controls on the whole page are the header search box (which just navigates away) and hover states. Every competitor lets you poke: pick a champion, flip a lane, see a number move. Here, the one place the site actually proves it has data — the explorer and the tier lists — is on classic.html, one click away and therefore invisible to the person deciding in the first ten seconds whether this is worth downloading.

Worse, the thing being sold is a panel that fills itself in during champion select, and the homepage represents that with an empty styled placeholder because the screenshot has not been taken. So the single most desire-creating asset the project owns — a live panel that answers instantly for any of 63 champions in any of 5 lanes, with sample sizes attached — sits unused in site/data/*.json while the page shows a grey box captioned "The app".

The fix is not another screenshot. It is to run the product's core panel in the page. Pick a champion, pick a lane, and the visitor gets exactly what the app hands them at lock-in: win rate against a 50%-origin bar, lane rank, pick rate, average KDA, the five most-built items with pick and win rates, boots, the summoner spell pair, and the three matchups they beat and the three that beat them — every line carrying the games it came from. That converts "125,096 games" from a claim into something the visitor personally interrogated, and it demonstrates the software by being the software. Nothing is invented: every figure is read straight from champions.json and builds.json, and only lanes flagged `qualified` are offered, so the demo can never open on a forty-game sample.

area: Feature showcase — KENMERKEN / kenmerkBlok in site/build.mjs (renders on index.html "Six things it does" and on app.html)
diagnosis: Six blocks, and five of the six frames are literally empty: `.kenmerk-beeld:has(.kenmerk-wacht)` draws a dashed rectangle over graph paper with the words "Screenshot in progress" inside it. So the one section of the homepage that exists to prove the software works currently proves that it does not exist yet. The copy next to each frame is excellent and specific — "objective timers", "items ranked by what actually won", "sample size attached, always" — and every single claim it makes is then illustrated by nothing. A reader who wants to believe you has no way to. Worse, the emptiness is unevenly distributed: as screenshots land one at a time (builds.png and matchups.png arrived while I was working), the section becomes a mix of real product and dashed placeholders, which reads as an unfinished page rather than a product tour. And the deeper miss: this project owns 125,096 games and a source tree with the real objective constants in it, so four of these six features can be *demonstrated* in HTML right now without waiting for a single screenshot. The placeholder was never the only option — it was the option that required no data. The fix is to make the frame a window with chrome and a provenance caption, put the screenshot in it when there is one, and when there is not, put a working slice of the feature in it drawn from the real files: Warwick's actual champ-select matchups, the actual respawn windows the overlay counts, Ezreal's actual top four items, one actual matchup that splits 10 points across two lanes, Tryndamere's actual five lanes with the one that gets no number, and the actual line counts of matches.jsonl.

area: The champion pages — guidePagina (63 with Classic data) and catalogusPagina (110 without)
diagnosis:
These are the deepest pages on the site and the most likely landing point from a search for "nasus classic build", and today they leave most of their own data on the floor.

The guide page has one hero (games, win rate, a lane name), a tab strip that shows one lane and hides four, and per-lane tables. Nothing on it is comparative, and comparison is the entire product. Concretely:
- champions.json already carries `kda`, `winrateRaw`, `strongestLane` and, per lane, `rank`/`rankOf`. `kda` is never rendered on the champion page. `rank #38 of 57` is printed once as bare text with no scale — it does not say whether #37 is a hair away or eight points away.
- An item row reads "The Black Cleaver — 57.3% held, 53.1% win". 53.1% of what? It reads as "good item". The number that makes it mean something — Lee Sin's own 46.7% in the jungle — is on the same page, six lines up, and the two are never put beside each other. Every item, boot, starter, spell pair and matchup row on all 63 pages has this problem: a win rate with no baseline is decoration.
- The 50 matchup rows per page name champions whose pages already exist and are not links. 63 deep pages, each a dead end.
- "Where does this champion belong?" — the one question people arrive with — costs four clicks, because four of five lanes are hidden behind tabs.

The 110 catalogue pages are worse: they open with a headline that apologises ("No win rate here yet, and that is the honest answer"), spend two paragraphs on why there is nothing, print six unranked base numbers, and stop. A page whose loudest statement is what it does not have cannot create desire, and it exits nowhere.

The fix uses no new data. Every number below already exists in champions.json, builds.json or lol-catalog.json; it is arithmetic and adjacency on values the build already reads.
